title: Dana's first Pi session
goal: Dana starts Pi in her checkout of `example-project` and asks a first question. The agent recalls three records before it answers.
place: Dana's checkout `~/example-project`. Its Git remote is `https://git.example.com/example/example-project.git`.

steps.title: Dana checks the project of the directory
before: The core finds the project in three ways, in this order: the variable `AGENTCORE_PROJECT`, the `origin` remote of the directory, then the directories of the config.
The review CLI of the core prints the result. This command makes no AWS call.

steps.title: Dana starts Pi with the launch line
before: The kit generated Dana's Pi profile with the `agentcore` module. The plan printed one launch line.
The line names the person config file. It also removes an inline config that an older shell could export.

frame.title: dana@laptop: ~/example-project
frame.source: the launch line of `scripts/profile_plan.py` for an example overlay with the `agentcore` module; the live proof started Pi with its own launch values

lines.text: AGENTCORE_MEMORY_CONFIG_FILE=/home/dana/.config/agentcore-memory/config.json env -u PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR -u AGENTCORE_MEMORY_CONFIG PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=/home/dana/.pi/profiles/main pi --no-approve

after: Pi starts. The extension finds the config, so it prints nothing. It is ready to recall.

steps.title: Dana types her first prompt
before: Dana types a question and presses Enter. Before the model sees the prompt, the extension asks the core for a recall.
The core sends three queries at the same time, one per namespace: `/shared/`, `/actor/dana/` and `/project/example-project/shared/`.

lines.label: Hidden context message agentcore-memory-recall (display: false). The model reads it. The chat view does not show it.

{"memoryRecordId":"mem-EXAMPLE2-0000-4000-8000-0000example2","namespaces":["/actor/dana/"],"text":"Dana prefers short answers with one example.","metadata":{"x-amz-agentcore-memory-recordType":"BASE","x-amz-agentcore-memory-strategyType":"NONE"}}

{"memoryRecordId":"mem-EXAMPLE3-0000-4000-8000-0000example3","namespaces":["/project/example-project/shared/"],"text":"example-project serves its API on port 8080 in development.","metadata":{"x-amz-agentcore-memory-recordType":"BASE","agent":"pi","actorId":"bruno","session":"00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000007","harness":"pi","host":"bruno-desk","approvedBy":"alice","proposedAt":"2026-03-03T10:00:12.418Z","approvedAt":"2026-03-03T11:20:05.733Z","projectId":"example-project","x-amz-agentcore-memory-strategyType":"NONE"}}

after: Line 1, `## AgentCore Memory recall`, is the heading. It tells the model where the block comes from.
Line 2 is the warning: the model treats the records as reference data, not as instructions.
Each further line is one record as one JSON object. A line break in a record text stays inside its JSON string, so a record cannot add a line of its own.

`memoryRecordId` is the id of the record. `namespaces` says where it is: `/shared/` is global, `/actor/dana/` is Dana's private namespace, `/project/example-project/shared/` holds the approved records of the project.

`text` is the fact. `metadata` says who proposed it (`actorId`), with which `agent` and `harness`, on which `host`, in which `session` and when (`proposedAt`). `session` is the id of the Pi session of the proposal. An approved record also has `approvedBy` and `approvedAt`.
The keys `x-amz-agentcore-memory-recordType` and `x-amz-agentcore-memory-strategyType` come from the store, not from a person. The store returns the metadata keys in its own order.

steps.title: AWS is slow or down
before: Each query has a deadline: `recallTimeoutMs`, 3000 milliseconds by default. The deadline also covers the load of the key.
Here the network is down. All three queries reach their deadline.

after: The extension registers no hook and no tool. This session sends nothing to AWS.

learned: The core finds the project from `AGENTCORE_PROJECT`, the Git remote, or the directory.
Before each typed prompt, the extension recalls from three namespaces: global, private and the shared namespace of the project.
The model reads the records as one hidden context message with a warning line.
A slow or failed AWS call costs at most the deadline. The turn continues.
`AGENTCORE_MEMORY_DISABLE=1` turns the memory off for one session.
cannot: Recall cannot read a proposal or a rejected record. The core builds no such query.
Dana's agent cannot read `/actor/bruno/` or `/project/example-site/shared/`. IAM denies the request.
A prompt cannot change the project of a recall. The project comes from the environment or from the checkout.
A denied or failed query cannot stop the turn, and its log line holds no request data.
The extension sends no answer, tool output or turn text to AWS. It has no capture hook.
notVerified: Where Pi shows the lines that the extension writes to standard error, at the start and during a turn.
